name: Ahio
overview: Ahio was a male member of the tribe of Benjamin, identified specifically as the son of Jeiel and Maacah. His mention in Scripture is brief and does not include additional notes or narrative beyond his lineage. This establishes him as a figure rooted in the genealogical records of Israel.
namesAndTitles: The name Ahio means '[my] brother is y-h-v-h,' reflecting a theophoric element that acknowledges the LORD (Yahweh) in his identity. This proper name is not indicated as given directly by God but carries a meaningful connection to the divine name, emphasizing a familial relationship with God.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture records Ahio as the son of Jeiel and Maacah, firmly situating him within a specific family line in the tribe of Benjamin. No other family relationships are documented beyond this explicit mention.
scriptureSignificance: Ahio's significance lies primarily in his genealogical placement within the tribe of Benjamin, as preserved in the chronicler's record. His mention helps to maintain the continuity of the Israelite lineage, which is vital for understanding the historical and spiritual heritage of God's people. While not prominent in narrative events, his inclusion underscores the faithfulness of God in preserving His covenant people through successive generations.
